correctness.rationale: For finite supported hypergraphs, maps from Box-hypercubes reduce exactly to graph cubical chains of the 2-section P(H). In degree one, oriented backtracks, triangles and 4-cycles generate all boundaries of cubical 2-cubes, identifying H1^Box(H;Z) with H1 of the 2-complex T(P(H)) filling all 3- and 4-cycles. The incidence-transposed hypergraph has 2-section equal to L(H), the edge-intersection graph. Replacing consecutive vertex-pair steps by incident-hyperedge witnesses transfers closed walks P(H)→L(H); changing witnesses differs by triangles and a 3- or 4-cycle transfers to a null-homologous short loop. Transposition gives the reverse map; the composites differ only by traversals within hyperedge cliques, hence triangles. This is an integral inverse, including torsion. Independently built graph short-cycle presentations and verified Smith H1 ranks: loose five-cycle Z on both sides, loose four-cycle zero, Fano zero. Tests support but do not prove arbitrary hypergraphs.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks do not establish the universal theorem without the analytical/chain argument given; code proof obligations were reconstructed separately.
